name: MySQL client flaw
tile_line: Rated 9.1, no details or exploit; security releases out.
tldr: Oracle rated a MySQL "Client programs" bug 9.1 but hasn't said how it works or who is at risk. No exploit or attacks are reported. On 8.4, 9.7 or 26.10, install Oracle's free fixed release; MySQL Cluster, 8.0 included, gets fixes on 26 Nov.
summary: Of the two GitHub "exploits" going around, one is a read-only version and exposure check; the other claims to exploit this CVE, but its author hadn't seen Oracle's fix, so that link is unverified.

affected.label: MySQL 8.4, 9.7, 26.10 or Cluster 8.0
affected.text: Oracle lists MySQL Server 8.4.0 to 8.4.13, 9.7.0 to 9.7.4 and 26.10, and MySQL Cluster 8.0.0 to 8.0.50, 8.4.0 to 8.4.13, 9.7.0 to 9.7.4 and 26.10. Server 8.0 isn't listed because Oracle no longer supports it, not because it was checked, so TuxCare treats it as possibly affected. Oracle files the bug under "Client programs", so machines with only the `mysql` command-line tools count too. MariaDB and Percona haven't said whether they're affected; Red Hat lists its hardened MariaDB 10.11 and 11.8 images as affected.

affected.label: An attacker reaches the MySQL traffic
affected.text: Oracle's patch table lists the protocol as "MySQL Protocol", but its CVE record says "network access via multiple protocols"; both say no login and no user action are needed. It hasn't said whether the server or a client program connecting to a server is the side at risk. "A client connecting to a malicious server" is analysts' guess, not something Oracle has confirmed. The sources also disagree on the kind of bug: CISA's data says improper authentication (CWE-287), Red Hat says missing authentication (CWE-306).

do.label: Update to the fixed release
do.text: Oracle released MySQL Server 8.4.13.1, 9.7.4.1 and 26.10.0.1 on 24 Nov 2026, free to download. Each release note calls it "a Critical Security Patch Update" and points to Oracle's November advisory, which lists versions up to 8.4.13, 9.7.4 and 26.10 as affected; the notes don't name this CVE. Update servers and machines with the `mysql` client tools. Oracle hasn't committed to a fix for Server 8.0, which it no longer supports. Debian, Red Hat and Ubuntu have no fixed packages yet; Red Hat rates it Critical, Ubuntu Medium.

do.label: MySQL Cluster: fix due 26 Nov
do.text: Oracle lists MySQL NDB Cluster 8.0.51, 8.4.13.1, 9.7.4.1 and 26.10.0.1 with a 26 Nov 2026 date; they aren't out yet. Update Cluster to them when they are.

do.label: No exploit or attacks yet
do.text: There's no confirmed exploit and no reported attack, it isn't on CISA's exploited list, and CISA's own assessment says exploitation "none". The 19 Nov GitHub code is a fake MySQL server that captures passwords from clients connecting without encryption; it claims to exploit this CVE, but its author hadn't seen Oracle's fix, so that link is unverified. We'll update the page if Oracle, the researcher or a distro explains the bug, and raise the verdict if real exploit code or attacks appear or it lands on CISA's list.

do.label: Optional: general hardening
do.text: TuxCare suggests limiting ports 3306 (and 33060 if the X Protocol is on) to the hosts that need them, having clients check the server's certificate with `--ssl-mode=VERIFY_IDENTITY`, and turning off local file loading with `--local-infile=0` where nobody uses it. It notes these are general hardening steps, not confirmed fixes for this bug.
